anomaly_def.Name: Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Exhaustion of physical or logical storage space allocated to data files, logs, temp areas, or backups, resulting in allocation-failed or no-space errors.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Exhaustion of kernel-enforced limits such as file descriptors, shared-memory segments, semaphores, or process/thread quotas, preventing the database from obtaining necessary OS resources.

When both conditions arise simultaneously, the database may encounter a compound failure mode: writes, log switches, temporary-object growth, or backup operations stop because storage is full, while at the same time new sessions, background workers, or file opens fail due to OS-level limits. Observable symptoms include a rapid succession of "no space left on device" and "too many open files" errors, stalled checkpoints that cannot flush dirty pages, archiver or logger processes that crash or hang, backup jobs that start but abort immediately, and connection storms where existing sessions hang in I/O wait while new logins are refused. Monitoring dashboards may show normal CPU usage yet a steep rise in transaction latency and an abrupt drop in throughput, making root-cause isolation difficult.

Causally, the two root causes can reinforce each other: log or temp spills caused by space pressure force the engine to open additional files, exhausting file-handle limits; conversely, reaching the file-handle or shared-memory ceiling can block housekeeping tasks (log rotation, purge, auto-extend) that would otherwise release or allocate new space, accelerating disk exhaustion. Attempts to auto-extend datafiles fail first on OS limits (unable to create or open the next file) and then on physical space scarcity, leading to cascading transaction aborts. The interaction traps the system in a feedback loop where neither space nor OS resources can be reclaimed, pushing the database into partial or complete outage until both constraints are relieved.

entry.official_definition: Maximum amount of time allowed to complete client authentication; if not completed in time, the server closes the connection.
entry.trigger_condition: A would-be client does not complete the authentication protocol within authentication_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the connection attempt, preventing hung clients from occupying a connection indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
